review_independence: Only assigned complete rules/LTP/FAQ, original printed components/provenance, and seven permitted candidate JSON files read. No summary, reader, grade, other reviewer report or web browsing read. Candidate map fields are validated against exact questions; historical verdict labels do not supply authority.

records.question: Describe complete core setup: which decks are separated, how the starting city and turn track are determined, the initial round/resource/threat/capital positions, corporation sides and cards, rival allocation, and the initial investment choice. Exclude the simplified first-game setup.
actual_asked_facts: Separately shuffle the four non-action decks and five action decks.
Random setup card determines listed city placements and facedown asset count in ascending turn slots; box all setup cards.
Round 1, resources 0, threat 0; reveal demand and set its target tokens.
Choose corporations, matching faceup emergencies and correct player-count sheet sides; draw initial sheet cards.
Random active player starts at 10 capital; clockwise players start at 11, 12, and so on.
Use participating-corporation rivals plus Federalist; secretly deal one each and put extra partly under board.
Each draws two investments, keeps one facedown and returns other facedown to top; form reserve.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Shuffle asset, demand, event and investment decks separately and separate/shuffle the five action types. Draw one shuffled setup card, placing one listed component in each listed district and its upper-right count of facedown assets on turn slots starting at1; box all setup cards. Round1, resources0, revealed demand targets as printed, threat0. Choose corporations and correct4 or5–6 side, matching faceup emergency, draw sheet cards. Random capital token chooses active player, who starts10 capital; clockwise11,12,etc. Shuffle used-corporation rivals plus Federalist, deal one secretly each, set extra partly under board. Each draws2 investments, keeps1 facedown, returns other facedown to deck top; create reserve.
source_refs: RR p2 Complete Setup steps1–12; RR21.1

records.question: What action cards does each corporation draw in four-player and five/six-player games, in what order, and how are General draws selected? Include Melange.
actual_asked_facts: Five specialists draw two of their specialty first: Globalsec security, Haas labor, Jinteki biotech, NBN media, Weyland construction.
At four players each specialist next draws one General; at five/six next types respectively media, construction, labor, biotech, security.
Melange has three separate one-General entries at either count, from three distinct decks.
Follow sheet top to bottom; General entry uses one deck not already drawn this Refresh, chosen before looking.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Globalsec2security, Haas-Bioroid2labor, Jinteki2biotech, NBN2media, Weyland2construction, followed by1General in4-player games. In5–6 these second draws are respectively1media,1construction,1labor,1biotech,1security. Melange draws1General three times in both sizes, each from a different type. Follow printed top-to-bottom order; choose a General deck not already drawn this Refresh before looking.

records.question: Describe the active player’s turn, including start-of-turn asset timing, Refresh, end-of-turn abilities, hand limit and passing. When does the Action Phase end and must every player have a turn that round?
actual_asked_facts: Start-of-turn assets resolve before Refresh.
Refresh readies exhausted assets, then draws sheet cards; resolve one deal.
Optional End of Turn abilities each once, then active player discards to ordinary hand limit five, excluding emergencies, then passes left.
Empty turn track at turn end ends Action Phase and leads to Production.
Turn count comes from setup/event, so some players can receive no turn that round.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Start-of-turn assets before Refresh. Refresh readies exhausted assets then draws sheet cards. Resolve one deal. End-of-turn abilities optional once per ability in chosen order; discard excess action cards to hand size5, then pass left. Emergencies do not count. When no turn-track assets remain at turn end, proceed to Production. Turns fixed by setup/event, not player count; some players may have no turn this round.

records.question: List the five deal steps and the order of effect, asset claim and cleanup. Which asset is revealed and can the active player pass on the main offer?
actual_asked_facts: Five steps in order: Asset, Main Offer, Counteroffer, Support, Resolution.
Reveal rightmost/highest-numbered turn-track asset.
Active player must propose a main offer and cannot pass.

Winner resolves offer before claiming revealed asset faceup, followed by cleanup: ordinary played actions facedown to shared discard; emergencies to original owners facedown if winning, faceup otherwise.
contextual_background: Clockwise one-chance counter/support details and support tie rule are correct additional explanation, tested in Q05/Q06, not required by a request to list the five steps.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Reveal highest-numbered/rightmost turn-track asset. Active player must propose one faceup hand action or faceup emergency; cannot pass. Others each get one clockwise counteroffer chance from active player’s left. Supporting players each get one clockwise support/abstain chance. Most facedown support wins, main offer wins ties. Winner resolves offer then claims asset faceup; all played action cards discarded facedown to shared pile, emergencies returned to original owners face down if winning, face up otherwise.

records.question: The first, second and third counteroffers are proposed in one deal. How many hand cards must each proposer discard in addition to their offer? Can the active player counter, can an earlier proposer later support, and is there another circuit of counteroffers?
actual_asked_facts: First, second, third counteroffers cost zero, one, two extra hand cards respectively.
Active player cannot counter without explicit permission.
Superseded proposer becomes eligible supporter if neither active nor current countering player.
Each nonactive player gets one chance, with no second circuit.
contextual_background: Only topmost offer remains operative is background here; explicitly asked in Q79.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Costs0,1,2 hand cards respectively based on earlier faceup cards in Counteroffer box. New offer covers earlier ones; only topmost remains operative, earlier ones only set cost. Active player cannot counter without explicit card permission. Earlier proposer becomes supporting player if neither active nor current counterer. No second circuit; each nonactive player gets one chance.

records.question: In a deal with a counteroffer, who may support, how are cards committed and counted, may a player support both or add more later, and who wins a2–2 tie? What happens if nobody counteroffers?
actual_asked_facts: Supporters exclude active and current countering player unless an ability overrides.
One clockwise chance from active player's left: abstain or place one or more hand actions facedown beside one offer.
Count cards, not card effects; no split between offers or later top-up.
A two-two tie goes to active player.
Without a counteroffer skip Support and resolve main offer.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: All except active and current counterer support unless ability explicitly overrides. Each once clockwise from active’s left chooses one or more hand actions facedown to one offer or abstains; cannot support both or add in another chance. Count cards, not printed effects;2–2 goes to active. If no counteroffer skip Support and resolve main offer.
source_refs: RR16.4–16.6,59–60; FAQ Deals; LTP p10 step4

records.question: How can an emergency be proposed or used as support, does it count toward hand size or hand-card theft, and where/state does a stolen emergency return after winning or losing an offer? What may Bryan Stinson steal?
actual_asked_facts: Only faceup emergencies may be main offers/counteroffers; emergencies never support.
Emergency is outside hand, does not count toward hand size and cannot be stolen by ordinary hand-action theft.
Stolen emergency returns to original logo corporation, facedown after winning or faceup after losing; facedown cannot be offered until flipped.
Bryan can steal two emergencies from participating corporations, either face orientation, preserving orientation.
contextual_background: Protection from ordinary hand-card discard is correct but not separately asked; Bryan claim/discard activation cost is not asked by what he may steal.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Only faceup emergency can be offered as main/counteroffer; never support. Outside hand, no hand-size count or ordinary hand steal/discard. Bryan can steal2 emergencies of participating corporations, faceup or facedown preserving state. Discarded/proposed stolen emergency returns to original logo corporation, face down if winning, face up otherwise; winning face down cannot be offered until flipped by effect.
source_refs: RR21,30.1; printed Bryan Stinson asset; LTP p14

records.question: An exploited district prints primary2 credits and secondary1 entertainment, has a development, an orgcrime unit and is in protest. What does it produce and what is its resulting unrest? How would starting in strike or outage change production, and do non-android districts produce in the normal Production Phase?
actual_asked_facts: Produces zero credits and one entertainment: orgcrime blocks developed primary, protest permits production.
Produce before protest rises to strike.
Starting strike or outage produces no resources.
Only android districts produce in ordinary Production.
contextual_background: Alternate starting unrest outcomes and ascending district order are not additional asked facts.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Produces0credits and1entertainment: development adds1 to primary but orgcrime blocks primary entirely; protest allows production. After producing, protest becomes strike. Starting strike or outage produces nothing but still exploited if android; strike remains strike and outage remains stable/outage absent Human First. Only districts with androids normally exploited, lowest-numbered first.

records.question: When an android district with Human First is exploited, what happens from stable, protest, strike, and already-outage starting states? Is an ordinary failed unrest increase without Human First enough to cause an outage?
actual_asked_facts: From stable, Human First exploitation raises unrest two stages to strike.
From protest or strike, inability to rise two places outage and clears unrest to stable.
Already-outage district is still exploited; newly generated duplicate outage must move.
Ordinary capped unrest increase without Human First exploitation does not place outage.
contextual_background: Production occurs before unrest, but no production quantity is requested by the state-branch question.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Produce first under existing modifiers. Human First adds2 unrest stages: stable becomes strike; from protest or strike cannot rise2, place outage and remove unrest to stable. Already outage still exploited and new outage must move. Ordinary unrest at strike cannot increase but causes no outage; only exploited Human First has this overflow rule.

records.question: An orgcrime unit is placed into a district already containing orgcrime and its route then meets a prisec-protected district before eventually reaching the Root. Explain its movement, reserve/threat result and contract consequences. How do android moves differ?
actual_asked_facts: Incoming duplicate orgcrime follows exiting arrows toward higher numbers, continuing past duplicates and prisec until legal or Root.
Root is not a district; entering unit returns to reserve and adds two threat.
Movement out of districts and return at Root trigger no removal contract.
Android moves ignore arrows, go anywhere without an android, and resolve one at a time.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: New orgcrime must follow outgoing arrow to higher-numbered district, continue past same type or prisec until legal district or Root. Root not a district; return to reserve and threat+2. Movement out of districts and return at Root trigger no removal contracts. Androids instead may relocate to any district ignoring paths, one at a time, never into one already containing android.

records.question: When does illness add threat during an action, including chosen districts and failed placements/moves? If several ill districts are involved is the increase multiplied? Do production or events trigger illness, and what does an illness token entering the Root do?
actual_asked_facts: An action involves chosen districts, component placements/removals and moves into/out of districts, including blocked attempted destinations or component shortage.
One or more involved ill districts adds two threat total, not per district.
Chosen unrest districts qualify.
Production and events do not trigger illness's action effect.
Illness entering Root returns to reserve and separately adds two threat.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Action involves district if chosen or component moved in/out placed/removed, including attempted destinations blocked by components or exhausted reserve. At least one involved ill district gives+2 total, not per district. Unrest actions choose districts and qualify. Exploitation and events do not trigger illness effect. Illness entering Root separately returns reserve and adds2.

records.question: State each corporation’s contract payment and trigger, who may resolve the triggering action, and the important Haas-Bioroid, NBN, Root and Melange exceptions.
actual_asked_facts: Globalsec gains one per enemy removed; Jinteki two per illness removed; Weyland two per outage removed; NBN one per unrest stage decreased.
Haas gains two for one or more android moves, at most once per turn.
Non-Melange contracts require action resolution regardless of its resolver.
Movement/Root are not qualifying district removals; outage clearing unrest pays no NBN.
Melange gains three after event only if its entire threat increase is less than two, including Root spillover.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Globalsec1 per enemy removed from district; Jinteki2 per illness removed; Weyland2 per outage removed; NBN1 per unrest stage decreased; Haas2 when1+androids moved, at most once per turn. These require action resolution, irrespective of resolver. Moves and Root removals no district-removal contracts; outage removing unrest no NBN. Melange instead gains3 after event if threat increase over entire event below2, counting Root spillover as well as top effect.
source_refs: Printed corporation sheets both sides1–6; RR11,35.2,35.6,39.1; FAQ Contracts

records.question: What may players trade or give away, what items cannot be traded after the official erratum, and when are immediate, future-promise, disputed-binding and three-player trades binding? Does an exhausted traded asset ready?
actual_asked_facts: Capital, assets and promises can be traded anytime; gifts allowed.
Cannot trade actions, emergencies, investments, rivals or corp sheets after FAQ correction.
Immediate complete agreed trades bind; three-plus-player trades bind if all aspects immediate and simultaneous.
Future promises and unresolved pre-agreement binding disputes are nonbinding.
Exhausted traded assets remain exhausted.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Capital/assets/promises at any time, gifts allowed. Cannot trade actions, emergencies, investments, rivals, corp sheets. Immediately/completely fulfillable agreed trade binding; three+ players binding if all simultaneous/immediate. Future promises nonbinding, may renege; unresolved binding status before agreement means nonbinding. Traded exhausted assets remain exhausted.
source_refs: RR65; FAQ Trading and erratum65.5; LTP p14

records.question: Explain asset timing when several abilities share a timing, what is optional, when exhausted assets ready, and whether a newly gained End of Turn asset can be used this turn. How often can each End of Turn ability be used?
actual_asked_facts: Owner chooses order of own same-timing assets; multiple owners resolve clockwise from active player.
May and End of Turn abilities are optional.
Readying occurs at start of Refresh after start-of-turn triggers.
Each End of Turn ability once; an asset received during that step can be used then.
contextual_background: Exhausted assets cannot be exhausted again is correct but unasked here.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: One owner orders own same-timing assets; multiple owners resolve clockwise from active player. May and End of Turn abilities optional. Start-of-turn triggers before Refresh, which readies assets. Exhausted cannot exhaust again. End-of-turn ability once each, chosen order; one received during that step can be used that turn.

records.question: Give the full demand-round order, including what happens when only one resource misses its target, when supplies reset and unchosen investments go, and which steps are omitted in the third demand round.
actual_asked_facts: Score revealed investments before Pay Demand.
All resources meeting/exceeding demand succeeds; any shortage applies one printed failure threat increase.
Third demand ends after Pay Demand and omits last two steps.
Earlier demands reset supplies to zero, old demand to bottom, reveal next and set targets.
Return all investments and shuffle, draw two each, keep one facedown, return other facedown to top.
Advance to next standard round.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Score revealed investments before demand. If every resource >=target demand met no increase; any one below fails whole demand and adds printed threat once. Third demand ends immediately after this step, omitting reset/new demand/investment. Earlier demands reset every resource0, old demand bottom new top revealed targets set. Return all investments shuffle, each draw2 keep1 facedown other top facedown without reveal. Advance round to standard.

records.question: The third demand fails and pushes threat to25. Does investment scoring happen first, and who wins if the Federalist has25 capital? Contrast finishing that demand below25, a tie with your named rival, and having your own rival card at4 versus5–6 players.
actual_asked_facts: Investment scoring precedes failed demand.
Threat reaching 25 ends immediately; Federalist at 25 capital wins alone.
Normal below-25 ending loses Federalist and independently checks others' rivals.
Named rival must be strictly beaten; tie loses.
Own-rival requires strictly beating at least two others at four players or three at five/six.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Investment scoring first. Threat25 immediately ends game; only Federalist wins if>=25 (all others lose); below25 Federalist loses and each ordinary player independently checks rival. Named rival must be strictly beaten, ties lose. Own rival must strictly exceed at least2 others in4player,3 others in5–6; ties do not count.

records.question: Which information may players communicate about action hands, hand counts, rival cards, investments, hidden turn-track assets, and event cards seen through a reorder effect? What does Thomas Haas require you to announce?
actual_asked_facts: Do not communicate hand identities or lie about hand count.
Rival cards cannot be revealed/discussed during play; reveal all at game end.
Investments remain facedown until scoring; unchosen investments are not revealed.
Hidden turn-track assets cannot be inspected.
Privately seen event fronts stay secret; event backs including top card are public.
Thomas user openly announces whether the rival swap occurred.
contextual_background: Investment-deck inspection prohibition is correct supporting information, rather than an extra communication requirement.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Cannot tell hand identities or lie about hand count. During play, rivals cannot be revealed or discussed; all players reveal rivals when the game ends. Investments stay facedown until demand; deck cannot inspect after deal and unchosen not revealed. Turn-track assets cannot inspect. Event fronts seen privately kept secret; backs including top public. Thomas user must openly state whether swapping under-board rival with own; occurrence public.

records.question: Where do discarded action cards, assets and removed components go? What happens if an action deck is empty when a card must be drawn, a reserve component runs out, or production would pass the track end?
actual_asked_facts: Actions go facedown to shared discard; assets facedown to asset-deck bottom; removed components to reusable reserve.
Empty required action deck: shuffle entire discard, reveal/sort types, shuffle each into corresponding deck.
No reserve component means do not place it.
Resources stop at final track space.
contextual_background: Cannot inspect facedown action discards and supply zero floor are correct background; the question asks destinations/reshuffle/upper cap.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Actions facedown shared discard, never inspect facedown discard. Assets facedown deck bottom. Removed components reserve reusable. Empty requested action deck: shuffle entire shared discard, reveal/sort by type then shuffle each into own deck. No reserve component means do not place. Resources stop at final space, cannot reduce below0.

records.question: How are a standard round’s phases ordered, which districts get exploited and in what order, and how is an event resolved, discarded and used to set the next turn track? Must that track be reset after the sixth standard round?
actual_asked_facts: Standard phase order Action, Production, Event.
Exploit all android districts in ascending district number.
Top event resolves top to bottom: upper effect, one component per listed district, lower-right asset count to lowest slots facedown.
Event goes to bottom; advance round.
No need to reset turn track after sixth standard round.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Action then Production (android districts ascending number) then Event. Reveal top event and resolve top to bottom: upper effect, listed components one per listed district, printed lower-right number of assets from deck onto lowest slots facedown. Event bottom of event deck, advance round. No need reset after sixth since no next Action Phase.

records.question: Is resolving Liquidation exploitation, and which production modifiers apply? How do Unorthodox Knowledge and Caprice Nisei interact, including whether the resolving player is bound by the announced resolution?
actual_asked_facts: Liquidation produces without exploiting; do not add normal exploitation consequences.
Orgcrime is explicitly ignored; development and supply caps still apply.
Caprice cannot affect Unorthodox Knowledge; its resolver is not bound by their stated resolution.
contextual_background: Target must not be strike/outage and printed final strike remain true; the question does not request full Liquidation text.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Liquidation chooses a district not in strike or outage, produces its resources without exploiting it, ignores orgcrime for that production, and then explicitly raises its unrest to strike. No normal exploitation consequences apply in addition to its printed effects. Development and supply caps still apply. Unorthodox Knowledge cannot be affected by Caprice Nisei, and its resolver is not bound by their stated resolution.

records.question: What is the per-district limit for androids, developments, illnesses, outages, prisec, Human First and orgcrime? Can Human First and orgcrime coexist, which duplicate incoming components move, and may the spare fourth android be added to play?
actual_asked_facts: At most one each android, development, illness, outage, prisec, Human First, orgcrime in a district.
Different enemy types may coexist absent prisec.
Incoming duplicate enemies/illness/outage move; android cannot enter occupied android district; development does not move.
Fourth android is replacement spare only.
contextual_background: Unrest does not move is correct extra information; unrest is not among this question’s named incoming duplicate components.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: At most1 of each named type per district. Different enemy types may coexist without prisec. Incoming duplicate enemy/illness/outage moves; development/unrest never move and android may not enter occupied android district. Fourth android is a replacement spare, not additional productive android.

records.question: A corporation has44 capital, then loses7. Where and which side is its capital token before and after? Do the bright multiples-of-five spaces award anything?
actual_asked_facts: At 44 capital token is 40-side on 4; after losing seven it is normal-side on 37.
Bright multiples of five have no mechanical effect.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: At44 use40-side at4. After losing7 total37, normal-side at37. Bright multiples5 confer no effect.

records.question: With Braintrust, what does four-player Globalsec draw and what is its hand limit? What does Melange draw, and may its doubled General cards all come from one type?
actual_asked_facts: Four-player Globalsec draws four security then two General from one nonsecurity deck and has hand limit four.
Melange draws three entries of two General, each entry from a different deck; not six of one type.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Globalsec4security then2General from a single nonsecurity type, hand4. Melange2General then2General then2General, three distinct types, two cards from each. Braintrust doubles each entry and reduces hand limit1.
source_refs: Printed asset3 Braintrust; corporation back0/both3; RR3.1,29,30

records.question: What changes when Floyd2X3A7C is claimed, and what is a normal player’s hand limit while owning it? If Floyd is gained by trade instead, is the five-card draw repeated and does the hand limit benefit apply?
actual_asked_facts: Claim Floyd: draw five actions of any types.
Ownership increases hand size by five to normal ten.
Trade is not claim, so no redraw but ownership hand benefit applies.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Claim draws5actions of any types. Ownership adds5hand size, normally10. Trade does not claim so no draw; hand-size benefit applies while owned.

records.question: What does Toshiyuki Sakai do when claimed, how many actions are drawn in total, and is the hand-size exception permanent?
actual_asked_facts: Discard Toshiyuki on claim to draw two of each of five action types, ten total.
No discard down to hand size this turn; exemption is temporary.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Discard him onclaim to draw2each of5types=10actions. Do not discard down to handsize this turn; it is a turn-specific exemption, not permanent increased limit.

records.question: At the start of another player’s turn, they have12 capital and Lily Lockwell’s owner has10. What may Lily do, is the stolen card random, when relative to Refresh, and what if both have10?
actual_asked_facts: At another player's start, 12 greater than 10 permits optional theft of one random hand action before Refresh.
Equal capital fails condition.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Owner may steal1random handaction before Refresh. At equal10 the more-capital condition fails so no steal.

records.question: When may Rachel Beckmann draw, including during another player’s deal, what hand condition and card type apply, and does a faceup emergency stop it?
actual_asked_facts: At end of each deal, including another player's, zero hand actions allows optional draw of one action of sheet's topmost type.
Faceup emergency is outside hand and does not prevent trigger.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: At end of eachdeal if hand0 maydraw1action of topmost sheettype. Not limited to ownturn. Emergencyoutsidehand doesnotprevent0condition.

records.question: Aaron Marrón’s owner proposes the third counteroffer; another player later proposes the fourth. How many extra cards are paid for each, where do those paid cards go, and does Aaron intercept support-card discards?
actual_asked_facts: Third counteroffer by Aaron owner pays two extra cards to ordinary facedown discard.
Fourth counteroffer by another player gives its three extra payment cards to Aaron owner instead.
Aaron does not intercept support cleanup discards.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Owner pays2extra toshared facedowndiscard as usual because Aaron onlyanotherplayer. Fourthproposer pays3cards toAaronowner insteadofdiscard. Aarononlycounterofferproposal costs, notsupport cleanup.

records.question: A supporting player abstains. When and at what cost can Eiko respond, and what choices must that player then make?
actual_asked_facts: When a supporter abstains during Support, Eiko owner may exhaust Eiko.
Abstainer must play one main-offer support card or lose one capital.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: At abstention owner may exhaust Eiko; abstainer mustplay1card supportingmain offer orlose1capital.

records.question: How does The Fall Guy allow an active player to make a counteroffer, what is discarded, what step follows immediately, and can Chief Gorman cancel that counteroffer?
actual_asked_facts: After own main offer, discard Fall Guy to propose own counteroffer.
Proceed immediately to Support, bypassing other counteroffer opportunities.
Chief cannot cancel this counteroffer.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Afterownmain offer maydiscardFallGuy toproposecounteroffer too. ProceedimmediatelySupport, noothercounterofferopportunities; Chiefcannotcancel thiscounteroffer.

records.question: When may Chief Gorman be used on an ordinary counteroffer, what payment avoids its return, and what happens to the proposer’s status, further counteroffers and already-paid proposal discards if returned?
actual_asked_facts: After ordinary counteroffer, optionally exhaust Chief; proposer avoids return by paying Chief owner two capital.
Returned offer goes to proposer's hand; proposer ceases countering, cannot counter again that turn, and receives no refund of proposal discards.
contextual_background: No universal stack, emergency-return interaction or previously displaced offer/player revival is asked or adjudicated. Chief printed cancellation, no repeat proposal, and RR15.8 status/sunk discards are the supported scope.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Afterproposal owner mayexhaustChief unlessproposergivesowner2capital. Returnedoffergoesproposerhand; losescurrentcounteringstatus,cannotcounteragainthatturn; proposalcostdiscardsnotrefunded.

records.question: For an ordinary offered action other than Unorthodox Knowledge, when and at what cost may Caprice Nisei act, and is the proposer then free to change the announced resolution?
actual_asked_facts: When an ordinary offer is proposed, optionally exhaust Caprice.
Proposer must declare exact resolution and is bound by declaration.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Whenplayerproposesoffer owner mayexhaustCaprice; proposer mustdeclareexactlyhowitwillresolve andisbound, cannotfreelychange.

records.question: At the start of Support, Isabel McGuire’s owner puts a deck card beside the counteroffer. Is the owner treated as supporting that offer, may an eligible owner then support the main offer normally, and does Locust Company’s restriction on that owner block Isabel’s deck card?
actual_asked_facts: Isabel's deck contribution does not make owner a supporter of that offer.
An eligible owner may normally support main offer or counteroffer.
Locust's hand restriction does not stop Isabel's deck contribution.
contextual_background: Timing at start of Support and deck contribution are scenario givens. Exhaust cost, choice of any deck and either-offer placement are correct card mechanics, not extra requirements asked by its three eligibility questions.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: OptionalexhaustIsabel atstartSupport places1topcardofanyactiondeck insupporteither. Doesnotmakeownerasupporterofchosenoffer. Ifeligible maynormal-supporteitherinclmain. Locustblocks handcounteroffersupport, notdeckviaIsabel.

records.question: When and at what cost does Locust Company restrict a player, which offer/card source is restricted, and may that player still support the main offer from hand?
actual_asked_facts: At start of Support optionally exhaust Locust and choose a player.
Chosen player cannot support counteroffer from hand; main-offer hand support remains legal.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: AtstartSupport owner mayexhaustLocust chooseplayer. Chosenplayercannotplayhandcards supportingcounteroffer; mainsupportfromhandallowed.

records.question: When are Midori and Tanaka used, what cost does each have, and which one requires a support tie? What winners may each choose?
actual_asked_facts: Midori exhausts when determining winner during Resolution, only on support tie.
Tanaka discards at start of Resolution, without needing a tie.
Each selects active or countering player to win.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Midori whendeterminingwinnerduringResolution, mayexhaust iftied, decidedealwinner(activeorcountering). Tanaka atstartResolution maydiscard chooseactiveorcounteringwinner withouttienecessary.

records.question: After a player proposes an offer, what may Mark Yale do, who becomes unable to trade, what kinds of trades are blocked, and for how long?
actual_asked_facts: After offer proposed, Mark owner may exhaust him.
Only proposer is barred from trading capital/assets until end of deal.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: Owner mayexhaustMark afteroffer; thatproposer cannottradecapital/assets untildealend. Otherplayersnotgenerallyblocked.

records.question: When using Naoko Watanabe, what is discarded and what is claimed? If the first gained asset has a when-claimed effect, does it wait until after the second claim?
actual_asked_facts: On claiming Naoko, discard her to claim top two assets one at a time.
Resolve first asset's when-claimed effect before second claim.
records.checked_fixed_key_outcome: OnNaokoclaim discardhertoclaimtop2assetsoneatatime. Firstwhenclaimed effectresolvesbeforesecondclaim.

records.question: Sunny LeBeau is present when one effect increases threat by3, and later an event sends two orgcrime units into the Root in separate instances. How many times can Sunny trigger in each case, what may be drawn each time, and does an exhaust cost apply?
actual_asked_facts: One three-threat increase gives one Sunny trigger; separate two Root entries give two.
